answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently audited work fails agreed checks. Splitting one attacker’s activity across a hundred names no longer creates free influence: every name must tie up capital, and detected fraud destroys part of it. A lotus, trellis, or sable may be a harmless handle, but none substitutes for collateral. The defense raises the cost of a Sybil swarm in proportion to its scale, while honest agents recover their stake after valid work.
